title: Chess Game Flaw
next_chapter_hook: When the 'news of death' of Chen Ji spread like a boulder thrown into a lake, the undercurrents of various forces began to surge—the mourning of Tianqing Sect, the probing of the Demonic Path, and the mockery of Xuanwu Sect would all arrive within three days.

text.content:
That flaw was so tiny it could almost be ignored, but Chen Ji's pupils contracted sharply—the fatal loophole of fate was actually hidden here.

He stared at the faint crack on the Tianji Record Fragment, his fingertips gently stroking the yellowed page surface. For three years, he had窥探天机 countless times, suffering the torment of the Heavenly Fate Value draining away madly, yet he never thought—the rules themselves were the greatest flaw.

Mo Xiansheng's voice rang out from the depths of the fragment, carrying a meaningful tone: "You found it."

"Death state." Chen Ji's voice was low and certain, "The Heavenly Eye cannot observe the fate of the dead."

He slowly stood up, moonlight spilling through the broken window lattice, casting light and shadow alternately across his face. For three years, he had thought he was the most insignificant piece on the chessboard, never realizing—the piece could also choose not to play this game.

dialogue.content:
Mo Xiansheng fell silent for a moment, the faint shadow of his remnant soul trembling slightly: "All seers throughout history died from peering into Heavenly Secrets. Do you think they understood why they rushed towards their doom?"

A cold smile curved Chen Ji's lips: "Because they only knew how to peek—and not how to hide."

text.content:
He turned and walked to the old wooden table, taking out a jet-black Jade Slip from the Hidden Compartment. That was what he obtained when the second page of the Tianji Record was unsealed—the "Heavenly Fate Concealment Talisman," capable of maintaining a death aura veil for one hour.

Three pieces.

He only had three.

But that was enough.

Chen Ji clutched the Jade Slip in his palm, his mind racing through every move ahead. The Heavenly Eye's observation came with a price—every gaze consumed its power. If it habitually tracked the fate trajectory of a "dead person" who always remained in a death state...

Its power would be wasted for nothing.

dialogue.content: "So—" Chen Ji murmured to himself, his eyes gleaming with dangerous light, "Let me teach Heavenly Dao how to play chess."

text.content:
He sat back by the window, taking out several transmission talismans from his chest. These were pieces he had secretly placed over the past two years—Outer Disciples/Servants from Tianqing Sect, fringe disciples from Xuanwu Sect, even a low-level scout from the Holy Sect.

Information, starting today, would be released in batches, by category, by volume.

First wave: "The废物 Chen Ji is dead."

choice.prompt: For the release timing of the first wave of intelligence, Chen Ji needed to make a choice—

choices.text: Tonight at midnight, three sects simultaneously
choices.description: Release Chen Ji's death news to all three major sects simultaneously at the same time, creating the maximum range of chaos, preventing forces from verifying in time.
choices.visible_cost: High risk: If any party sees through it early, the entire subsequent plan will be exposed
choices.visible_reward: Maximum chaos: Within three days, the three sects will generate countless suspicions and internal friction due to information asymmetry
choices.risk_hint: Once Tianqing Sect verifies the body early, everything is lost

text.content:
Chen Ji's fingertip flicked, activating three transmission talismans simultaneously, turning them into streams of light that vanished into the night.

Three sects simultaneously—the news would arrive at the same moment—this meant no single party could gain the advantage of "exclusive news" first. The information gap was flattened by his simplest and most brutal method.

choices.description: Release news sequentially in the order of Tianqing Sect → Xuanwu Sect → Holy Sect, at six-hour intervals, creating a compounding effect of information asymmetry.
choices.visible_cost: Longer waiting period: must maintain feigned death state for three days,精神紧绷
choices.visible_reward: Chain reversal: each party, upon learning the news, will believe they were the last to know, doubling the anxiety
choices.risk_hint: The longer the delay, the higher the exposure risk

text.content:
Chen Ji shook his head and chose the more prudent plan.

He activated the first transmission talisman, the stream of light flying east. Six hours later, Tianqing Sect would learn the news first—then Xuanwu Sect, and finally the Holy Sect. With each wave of news arriving, the receiver would think "others already know," and that anxiety of being left behind would make them panic.

Just as he prepared to activate the transmission talisman, a faint spiritual energy fluctuation suddenly came from outside the window.

Chen Ji's movement halted abruptly.

The spiritual energy fluctuation was extremely subtle—if he hadn't spent every night enduring hardship in this servant district for three years, he would never have detected it. Someone was watching him.

dialogue.content: "Senior Sister Su," Chen Ji spoke without turning, his voice calm to the point of mockery, "Since you're here, why hide outside the window catching the breeze? Come in and sit?"

text.content:
Silence stretched outside the window.

Then the window lattice was gently pushed open, and a cold figure fell into the moonlight. Su Qingyao wore a plain white Inner Sect uniform, her brows carrying a cold scrutinizing sharpness, yet when her gaze met Chen Ji's, she frowned slightly.

She smelled it.

There was a faint herbal scent in the air—that was the smell of "Fake Death Pill."

dialogue.content: "Chen Ji." Su Qingyao's voice was very soft, yet carried undeniable pressure, "What are you doing?"

text.content:
Chen Ji turned around, his face showing that usual timid expression—shoulders slightly slumped, gaze dodgy, like a rabbit being stared at by a beast.

But deep in his eyes, cold light flashed for an instant.

Three times.

This was the third time Su Qingyao had come infinitely close to the truth.

choice.prompt: Facing Su Qingyao's questioning, Chen Ji needed to decide how to respond—

choices.text: Continue pretending, show weakness to the end
choices.description: Maintain the废物 persona, let Su Qingyao think she's being paranoid, use her suspicious nature as a new protective coloring.
choices.visible_cost: Su Qingyao's suspicions will accumulate, harder to explain in the future
choices.visible_reward: The废物 image will be further solidified, Su Qingyao's testimony will反而 become cover
choices.risk_hint: She's already suspicious, pretending may backfire

text.content: "S-Senior Sister Su?" Chen Ji's voice trembled slightly as he hastily stuffed the Jade Slip into his chest, "I-I just couldn't sleep, got up to practice alchemy..."

dialogue.content: Su Qingyao stared at him, her gaze like a blade: "Practice alchemy? Do you think I can't smell the Fake Death Pill?"

choices.text: Half truth, half deception, reveal part
choices.description: Admit you're preparing a backup plan, but hide the true purpose deeper—let her think she sees through everything, when she's actually only seen the tip of the iceberg.
choices.visible_cost: The more Su Qingyao knows, the greater the future variables
choices.visible_reward: She will become your most loyal "accomplice," because she's already boarded this boat
choices.risk_hint: High-intelligence characters are hard to fool, exposed flaws may be remembered

text.content:
Chen Ji sighed, his shoulders slightly relaxing, that "废物 quality" fading a few degrees.

"Senior Sister Su's keen observation is indeed sharp." His voice calmed down, no longer pretending, "I'm preparing an escape route—someone wants to kill me, I need a feigned death backup. That's all."

Su Qingyao said nothing.

She simply watched Chen Ji quietly, her eyes reflecting the moonlight and some complex emotions. Three years—she had investigated for three years, smelling Fake Death Pill from a废物 servant—this fact itself was absurd.

A废物 doesn't need feigned death.

Unless that "废物" was never real to begin with.

dialogue.content: "Chen Ji," Su Qingyao suddenly spoke, her voice carrying a fatigue she herself wasn't aware of, "Who exactly are you?"

text.content:
In the moonlight, Chen Ji fell silent for a moment.

He raised his head, meeting Su Qingyao's gaze directly for the first time. Those eyes held no cowardice, no evasion, only an abyss-like darkness.

"Who am I?" he softly repeated, a meaning-laden curve forming at the corner of his lips, "Senior Sister Su, haven't you been investigating for three years?"

"Haven't found out yet?"

Su Qingyao's pupils contracted sharply.

This was the first time in three years that Chen Ji had directly responded to her investigation. He didn't deny, didn't evade, but in a manner近乎残忍, admitted that he had been acting all along.

The air seemed to solidify.

Then Chen Ji laughed.

dialogue.content: "Senior Sister Su, would you like—" his voice low and enticing, "to play a bigger game of chess with me?"

text.content:
Su Qingyao fell silent.

In the moonlight, her expression was complex beyond measure—there was anger, shock, unwillingness, but more than anything, a strange sense of... release?

Three years of investigation finally had an answer. Even though this answer was more dangerous and unpredictable than she had imagined.

choice.prompt: Su Qingyao's reaction was unexpected; Chen Ji needed to decide his next move—

choices.description: Show Su Qingyao part of the plan, formally incorporating her into his chess game—she is the Inner Disciple Senior Fellow of Tianqing Sect, and her intelligence network far exceeded his own.
choices.visible_cost: Exposing your trump cards—if she turns against you, it will be utter ruin
choices.visible_reward: Gain access to Tianqing Sect's core intelligence channels; Su Qingyao's investigative abilities will become the greatest asset
choices.risk_hint: Trusting someone who has investigated you for three years—is that too risky?

text.content: "Heavenly Dao wants to kill me." Chen Ji's voice was soft, yet every word was clear, "I need to survive, need time. And you—you happen to have what I need."

choices.memory_label: 苏青瑶第一次被邀请进入核心棋局

choices.text: Stop at the right point, keep your distance
choices.description: Only reveal the information that 'someone is chasing me,' but don't show the core plan. Let her think she knows everything, when she's actually only seeing the periphery.
choices.visible_cost: Lose a potential powerful ally, have no one to watch over you during feigned death
choices.visible_reward: Trump cards remain intact; even if Su Qingyao is used by the enemy, core secrets cannot be leaked
choices.risk_hint: She will continue investigating, potentially becoming a hidden danger in the future

text.content:
"Someone is hunting me." Chen Ji's voice returned to calm, "Senior Sister Su, if you really want to know who I am—help me survive this ordeal."

He paused, adding softly: "The rest, we'll discuss later."

Su Qingyao glanced at him deeply.

In the moonlight, that servant disciple she once considered废物 was now emanating a temperament she had never seen before—dangerous, calm, calculating with precision.

Is this his true face?

She suddenly understood—why for three years, no matter how she investigated, she could only touch that impenetrable fog.

"Chen Ji." Su Qingyao finally spoke, her voice carrying a softness she herself wasn't aware of, "I will be watching you."

Not "I will find out," but "I will watch you."

This was compromise, and also a kind of... acknowledgment.

Chen Ji watched her figure vanish into the night, the curve at the corner of his lips deepening slightly.

Three times.

Third time infinitely close to the truth, and third time he gently pushed her away. But this time, something was different—Su Qingyao was no longer a simple investigator; she had already begun... taking sides.

This was good.

The more pieces, the more exciting the chess game.

He turned back to the window and activated the transmission talisman in his hand.

Light streaked across the sky, vanishing into the northern night—that was the direction of Xuanwu Sect. The first wave of intelligence had been sent.

Next, he just needed to wait.

Wait for those who thought themselves chess players to discover they were actually also pieces.

Wait for the Heavenly Eye to discover that its observed subject... had already died.

Chen Ji slowly closed his eyes, a serene smile forming at his lips: "The chess game begins to reverse from today."
